speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Our travel agents play an important role in the tourism ecosystem as they deliver memorable experiences to both visitors and locals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: At the same time, the travel agent industry provides good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Since the Travel Agents Act came into force in 1976, MTI and STB had reviewed and amended the Travel Agents Act in 1993 and the Travel Agents Regulations in 2007 to ensure that the regulatory regime remains relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Compared to 10 years ago, the travel industry has evolved significantly, in particular, with the intensifying growth of e-commerce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Consumers can now browse and compare a wider range of travel products online on various platforms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: There is also greater demand for experiential travel that is immersive and authentic while personalised for consumers' needs and preferences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To keep up with these changes, many travel agents are seeking additional channels to reach out to customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Some of them have evolved from the traditional brick-and-mortar model to new operating models, or developed new and niche areas of business.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: It is thus timely for us to amend the travel agent legislation to take into account these emerging business models and ensure that consumers continue to be adequately protected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The majority of Singapore's travel agents provide quality travel experiences and contribute to a positive image of the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Unfortunately, there is a small minority that conducts their businesses irresponsibly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In this regard, STB regulates the travel agent industry through a licensing framework implemented via the Travel Agents Act and Regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The framework allows STB to take action against fly-by-night travel agents and provides safeguards against malpractices that pose risks to travellers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: At the same time, the Government works with the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) and industry associations to safeguard consumer interests.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In the course of our review, MTI and STB have sought feedback from more than 180 industry stakeholders, including a diverse group of travel agents, industry associations, tourist guides and CASE.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: With their valuable input, we had put forth a draft Bill for public consultation earlier this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The respondents were generally supportive and provided constructive input on how to facilitate more effective implementation on the ground.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: MTI and STB have carefully considered all feedback received and incorporated them where relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We have sought to balance consumer and business interests when finalising these amendments, which I will now outline.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: One key objective of this legislative review is to better protect consumers against potential malpractice by travel agents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Sudden closures that affect a larger number of consumers also remain a concern, even though these cases are infrequent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To address these issues, we have proposed the following amendments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Clause 6 highlights that in making licensing decisions, STB will consider additional factors, including whether the individuals involved with the travel agency, such as company directors, are suitable to hold the licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For instance, individuals who had previously contravened travel agent legislation might be denied licences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Second, the amendments seek to equip STB with sufficient investigation and enforcement powers, so as to enable them to take action against errant operators more promptly and effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Clause 10 enhances STB's investigation and enforcement powers, for example, by empowering STB to take photographs, audio and video recordings that may facilitate investigations and that can serve as evidence for any contraventions of the travel agent legislation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The show cause period is the period after STB issues the initial notice of suspension or revocation, during which the travel agent will have the opportunity to explain why they should be allowed to keep their licences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: If the travel agent is unsuccessful in making a case for retaining its licence, STB will issue the order of suspension/revocation after the show cause period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As travel agents are still able to conduct business and collect payments from customers during the show cause period, we have shortened the time required for STB to complete the licence suspension or revocation process, thus reducing the risk consumers are exposed to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The new 14-day period has been pegged to the provisions in other similar legislation, to ensure that licensees have a reasonable amount of time to present their case.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Fourth, we have adjusted the penalty amounts for contraventions of travel agent legislation, following their last update in 1993.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The amounts need to be sufficiently high to deter potential malpractice.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The maximum fine for other offences has also been doubled.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For compoundable offences, clause 18 provides for a maximum composition amount of half the maximum fine prescribed or $5,000, whichever is lower.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is an increase from the current maximum composition sum of $1,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Even as we raise the penalty ceilings in some cases, we are also conscious that penalties imposed should be proportionate to the severity of the contravention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Certain minor and technical contraventions will consequently be decriminalised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: STB will thus be able to take swifter and proportionate enforcement action against travel agents in such cases, instead of going through a lengthy prosecution process.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Another key plank of our efforts to enhance consumer protection measures is based on the principle of "caveat emptor", or "let the buyer beware".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: While we have made the relevant changes to empower STB to do more to ensure that travel agents are professional and responsible, it is, ultimately, the consumers who make the final purchasing decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In this light, we have also taken steps to ensure that travel agents will provide the information necessary for consumers to make informed purchasing decisions, with a greater awareness of the potential risks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: If required by STB, travel agents have to make this disclosure during the show cause or appeal periods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is important as travel agents are still able to collect payments from customers during these periods, when there is a chance that they may not be able to fulfil these obligations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: With this disclosure by travel agents, customers can take this information into account when deciding whether to continue transacting with the travel agent facing suspension or revocation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: STB may also publish the notice or order of suspension or revocation on its website, to further raise awareness of travel agents that are facing suspension or revocation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Taken together, the measures I have outlined above are a comprehensive suite of consumer protection measures that facilitates STB's role as the regulator, while also empowering consumers to make more informed purchasing decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: At the same time, we have also taken care to ensure that the regulatory regime remains fair to licensees, who will continue to have the right to show cause and not be subjected to overly punitive measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We want our travel agents to remain relevant and enhance their capabilities in meeting the rising demand for experiential and customised travel.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: To cater to travel agents with different areas of business, clause 6 provides for the creation of different classes of licences with different minimum financial requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This refers to tours that bring travellers around Singapore with dedicated transport provided to ferry the tour group around, including coach tours or bum boat tours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Niche licensees will be subjected to lower minimum financial requirements compared to general licensees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: While we have reduced the regulatory costs, we will still need to retain regulatory oversight over such niche licensees so as to protect consumers from possible errant operators who may carry out malpractices, such as forced shopping expeditions, or commonly known in the industry as "zero-fare tours".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We are also making a related amendment to the Travel Agents Regulations to calibrate the licensing regime according to different levels of risk posed to consumers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will exempt some entities from needing travel agent licences, such as entities who sell or arrange tours within Singapore without providing passenger-carrying conveyance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These tours tend to be more experiential as the participants operate the conveyance themselves, including bicycle tours, segway tours and kayaking tours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Walking tours will also fall under this category.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Such entities pose much lower risk to consumers as prepayment is typically low or not required.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We hope that this exemption will encourage more entities to offer consumers innovative and experiential tours and, in turn add to the vibrancy of our tourism landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As tour models constantly evolve, we will review the exemption from time to time to ensure that it remains relevant and balances innovation and consumer protection.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Collectively, these measures benefit entities who pose lower consumer risk, enabling them to obtain travel agent licences more easily and, in some cases, even exempting the need for a licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: By doing so, we hope to encourage more players to provide differentiated offerings to both tourists and locals, which will also help them to innovate, grow and maintain relevance in response to changing consumer preferences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: With greater innovation in our tourism options, there could also be more appealing and flexible jobs available to Singaporeans who wish to join the tourism sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: With these legislative amendments, we hope that the travel agent industry will be better positioned to grow and thrive in the fast-changing tourism landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Effective legislation is just one component of the Government's continual efforts to strengthen the regulatory framework.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The other key strategy is to step up our consumer education efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We will continue to work with all stakeholders, including the travel agent associations and CASE, to raise awareness of common malpractices and the benefits of purchasing travel insurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We hope that these efforts will help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, Parliamentary colleagues, there are currently close to 1,200 travel agents in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The majority of Singapore's travel agents are law-abiding and ethical operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, there are occasionally a few "black sheep" who tarnish the reputation of the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In such cases, the Government has to take action in accordance with the law to protect consumers' interest and safeguard the reputation of Singapore's tourism industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In order to better protect our consumers, the amendment Bill proposes the following key measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This will lower the chances of customers making misinformed decisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In addition, after taking into consideration recent developments in the tourism industry, the amendment Bill will reduce regulatory requirements on lower-risk travel operators to encourage them to roll out more innovative and attractive travel products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This can also help to create more attractive and flexible job opportunities for Singaporeans who wish to join the tourism industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Besides amending the Travel Agents Act and Regulations, STB will continue to work with industry players to strengthen consumer education, encourage consumers to buy travel insurance and raise awareness of the updated provisions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I hope that all Members will support these measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Sim Ann) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Even established brand names, like Five Star Travels, Asia Euro Travel, Ho Wah, S-Travel and MISA Travel, who have been in the travel business for many years, were unable to survive in the tough competitive business environment and, eventually, they ceased operations.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When they did cease operations, consumers who had made travel bookings and payment in advance were left in the lurch.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: There is nothing they can do when businesses fail; even lodging claims will not get back their payment because consumers are unsecured creditors and rank last.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As not all affected consumers lodge their complaints with CASE, these reported figures of 792 complaints may represent only a fraction of the total number of consumers affected by the closure of the travel agencies.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Many consumers, after finding out that the travel agency had ceased operations, do not lodge complaints to CASE because they know that they cannot recover their losses.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: CASE has been in constant dialogue with STB on the issue of closure of the travel agencies for the past few years.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Allow me to put on record my appreciation to STB officers for meeting us regularly and discussing consumer protection with myself and my CASE officers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the consultation paper put up by STB in June 2017, it was stated that STB will enhance consumer protection by amending the regulations governing the Travel Agents Act.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: One such amendment to the regulations will prohibit travel agents from publishing "inaccurate or erroneous" advertisements.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I welcome such an amendment as advertisements which contain inaccurate or erroneous details will be misleading to consumers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Thus, if a travel agent advertises its tours as "zero costs" and then recover its costs from consumers by imposing compulsory minimum spending or compulsory tips, that is clearly inaccurate and misleading.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also welcome clause 10 of the Bill which imposes a requirement for travel agents facing suspension or revocation of their licences to disclose this fact to new and existing customers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will allow consumers to be aware of the trading status of the travel agent.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Hence, it is for consumers to make an informed decision whether to continue dealing with the same travel agent facing the restriction.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For this particular clause 10, may I ask the Senior Minister of State to clarify: for consumers who had already bought travel packages from a travel agent facing suspension or revocation of their licences, can these consumers be allowed the option of terminating their contract without compensation or losses?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For CASE, our main concern is about consumer protection whenever a travel agency ceases operations.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Each time we read about a travel agency ceasing operations or had its licence revoked by STB, there will be losses suffered by consumers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And these figures exclude the sales recorded by some travel agencies which conduct pre-travel fair sales.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And for each sale of a travel package, consumers typically pay deposits of between 20% and 50% of the package costs.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Some consumers even pay for the entire package in full so as to obtain freebies from their credit card companies.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In response to our concerns about closure of travel agents, STB had implemented a policy that travel agencies must inform consumers about the importance and the need to purchase travel insurance.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Unfortunately, not every consumer buys travel insurance as the insurance costs add up to the overall costs paid for by the consumers.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, I would ask the Government to consider requiring travel agencies to provide a performance bond or insurance to protect against business failure.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: It is part and parcel of doing business, just like lawyers and doctors are required to provide insurance against claims by their clients.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And this, hopefully, will, at least, provide some form of protection for travellers who, for some reason or other, do not buy travel insurance.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also urge STB to constantly check on the financials of the travel agencies.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This will allow STB to better anticipate whether a travel agency may be facing financial difficulties and, thereafter, STB can step in to protect the deposits paid by consumers as early as possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I would also like to highlight another area, which is the prevalence of online travel portals like Agoda Travel, Hotels.com, Booking.com and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I understand that many of these companies are not registered in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In such a case, may I ask who regulates these online travel portals?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: In the event that these online travel agencies cease operations, how do consumers recover their payment made to such online travel companies?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Perhaps, the Government can consider introducing regulations to regulate online travel agents as well.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The Government should also consider an outreach programme to remind consumers who have bought their air tickets or hotels via such travel portal on the importance of purchasing travel insurance after making their booking.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Singapore also received 16 million visitors in 2016.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Clearly, it is important that we strengthen our legal provisions for travel agents which are a key pillar of the industry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The tourism industry has three key components: travellers, travel agents and workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While I agree with the amendments proposed in this Bill, I hope that the Ministry can also review three other areas of enhancements: protecting consumers, having stronger travel agents and having a good workforce of tour guides and workers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While many recreational travellers plan their own itineraries, there is still a strong demand for the services of travel agents as they are convenient.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In 2014, when Five Stars Tours suddenly closed down, customers were stranded and some only knew through reports in the media.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: STB has a website called Travel Related Users' System (TRUST) where the public can check on travel agents that have had their licences revoked or those companies that have ceased operations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This is useful, especially to prevent fraudulent transactions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It can be made more useful if companies with chequered customer service track records are also included.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This could be a result of a fundamental structural shift in the tourism industry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can the Minister share what are the main reasons for tour agents closing down?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The relatively large number of closures suggest that greater protection for both consumers and workers is needed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In fact, could this be used for all the net worth capital requirements for the licences?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: The tourist guides are largely freelancers engaged by the travel agents to bring the tourists around Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: When travel agents close, they are adversely impacted.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Most guides are not paid CPF or might not be covered under any insurance paid by the travel agent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: As the travel industry transforms, we need to ensure that the workers as well as the tourist guides are trained in the relevant future skills.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Digital skills, customer service, language abilities and emotional intelligence capabilities are increasingly valued highly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: What are the training plans that STB has in place to help the travel agents and tourist guides to upgrade and upskill their workers so that they can help to grow the tourism industry?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Could STB also consider having training content that is bite-size and on-the-go so that it is easily accessed by tourist guides who are often moving about as their work entails?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: As freelancers, their income would be affected if they are to take time off for training.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: So, formal learning can be difficult for them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: To ensure the professionalism of the tourism industry, the future skills of the tourist guides should be tested to renew their licences.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In addition, tourist guides go through a Mandatory Refresher Course (MRC) as part of the requirements for licence renewal.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: MRC is now conducted in both English and Mandarin.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This prepares for the future as Chinese tourists are expected to be an important group for the tourism industry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We must not forget the key markets, such as India and Indonesia.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In view of the changing landscape of the tourism industry, how is STB ensuring that the future skills of guides are developed when they renew their licences?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This Bill also proposes several measures to encourage greater innovation in travel products and services offered in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: One provision exempts low risk/incidental players from the licensing regime to foster innovative and varied tour options.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These measures will increase competition within the travel sector and will spur smaller agents and non-agents to be creative in coming up with programmes.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Airbnb, for example, has a platform for visitors to sign up for "Experiences" in the city.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: While there are some options offered in Singapore, such as hiking, bike riding and watercolour painting, the offerings are somewhat limited, compared to what one can get, say, in San Francisco, where you could pay $50 to explore Victorian buildings with an enthusiast on the topic.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: In New York, you can pay $71 to explore the Garment District with a local designer.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: These types of "off-the-beaten-track" tours give life, vibrancy and variety to the kind of experiences a visitor could have in a city.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Now, hopefully, with the change in provisions, more Singaporeans with knowledge or talent in different fields could come forward to offer such experiences.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: With regard to this change, I have two concerns.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: First, for those who are exempted from licensing, what kind of safeguards will there be against entities that are not providing legitimate services, or those who are out to scam visitors, or those who do not carry out their duties responsibly?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Will we just leave it to the market to give them poor ratings and regulate itself?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We must balance fostering a culture of innovation and Singapore as a reliable place for vacation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We are clearly in the correct direction with this Bill.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How do we ensure that the interests of consumers and tour guides and even staff who are engaged by the travel agents are safeguarded?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We want a healthy travel eco-system with honest players.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My question is: will the amendments make errant travel agents act more responsibly?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Or will it lead to a cat-and-mouse scenario whereby evading the regulators becomes the mode of operation?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am, therefore, keen to know if STB will have adequate manpower and authority to intervene and act when signs of early concerns are detected.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Minister earlier mentioned that they will be able to act more promptly.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But I think the need is to really focus on them coming in to rectify the issue rather than when major damage has been committed.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Apart from regulations, Mr Speaker, we also need to evolve a culture of co-ownership and investing to grow the industry.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Technological advances, coupled with changes in consumer travel habits, have seen the travel agent business evolve.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need to keep track of what is happening elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will STB help to equip our travel agents and tour guides with the necessary skills and tools in order to compete in an ever-changing travel and tourism landscape?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am glad to learn that this amendment will enable certain exemptions for travel agent businesses that are niche and unique in nature.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think that is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is a strong impetus for STB to rally industry stakeholders to co-drive the transformation for the travel industry.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In short, the authority cannot do it alone.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It requires the commitment and partnership of everybody in the travel industry.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope STB will have the staff to work alongside the travel industry's stakeholders to develop more professional agents and workforce.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These are industry development and capability development in nature, not necessarily enforcement.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A more professional travel industry will mean fewer instances of bad practices that will require regulatory intervention.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As they say, more dialogues can only mean more understanding and that is a good thing.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such a platform will enable views to be heard, even though they may be diverging.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Eventually, they will come to a convergence whereby it will be used to promote the betterment of the industry.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Beyond just ensuring that we have a healthy regulatory environment, Mr Speaker, we also need the right tools, the right people, the right players and the right culture.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Providing better consumer safeguards against errant travel agents, while balancing this with measures to facilitate a pro-business environment for the travel industry is welcomed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have comments and queries on two aspects of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Clause 19 expands the regulation-making powers of STB.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Amongst other things, this clause introduces a new section 28(1)(ga)(i) which confers powers on STB, such as "imposing restrictions or obligations on licensees in relation to any variation or termination of a contract for the supply by the licensee of a travel product".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MISA Travel closed in June 2017 and customers who had paid for travel plans and products were left in the lurch.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For illustration purposes, let us assume that a travel agent is not fraudulent and has a legitimate business.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, this travel agent suddenly shuts down or is unable to fulfil its primary contractual obligation of ensuring travel products are supplied to travellers for reasons whether in its control or not.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is often the situation that consumers face.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even if STB invokes the power in the new section to vary the contract or even direct that the said travel agent has to compensate or refund the travellers, it is unlikely that the travel agent can, will and want to be able to fulfil their obligation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the travel agent could, would and wanted to fulfil its obligations, there would not have been a need for STB to step in in the first place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Compensation Fund can be financed by all registered travel agents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While this will mean that travel agents have to pay into this fund, it is beneficial in the long term to instil consumer confidence considering that the travel industry is one of the top 10 most complained about industry, according to CASE.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This may help with providing a more robust regulatory framework and, eventually, re-direct much of the travel purchases and revenue back to travel agents, benefiting the travel agents.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This might also help in reversing the trend of travellers purchasing travel through direct channels.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: From a policy perspective, this Compensation Fund provides accountability and immediate practical recourse to travellers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that this is the model already adopted in Ontario, Canada, and Hong Kong.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do hope we can implement this in Singapore as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, what plans are there to regulate such businesses to ensure that travellers who purchase travel products via such businesses equally have consumer safeguards?

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Several Members raised queries and suggestions on dealing with this matter.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In such instances, there is typically minimal consumer impact, as these travel agents ceased operations after fulfilling all contractual obligations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Over the past three years, we have also noticed that around 40% of business cessations were by travel agents who were already dormant.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As such, we should not be overly alarmed by this kind of usual cessation of business.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As pointed out by Mr Lim Biow Chuan, the issue of concern is sudden closures.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: On this note, sudden closures remain relatively infrequent.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Nonetheless, every such closure can be a case of concern.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The case of MISA Travel was widely reported earlier this year, where the business decision was made to not continue operating.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In MISA's case, the business failure which resulted in its closure was not due to malpractice or any ill-intent on MISA's part.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The Government does not have regulatory oversight over such business decisions made independently by travel agents.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee asked for early intervention and Mr Lim Biow Chuan urged STB to constantly check on the financial health of our travel agents.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: STB conducts regular checks on the audited accounts of all licensed travel agents annually.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: While such checks can provide possible tell-tale signs of financial difficulties, we cannot safeguard against business failures.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: What the Government does is to monitor such closures very closely and work with CASE and other industry stakeholders to minimise consumer impact.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will also continue encouraging consumers to take measures to protect their interests by purchasing travel insurance that covers against travel agent insolvency.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Louis Ng asked how the new section 28(1)(ga)(i) would be helpful to consumers in cases of sudden closure, as even if STB varies the contract or directs that the licensee compensates consumers, travel agents might not be willing and able to do so.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Ang Hin Kee expressed concerns for the impact of sudden closures on tourist guides.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Thus far, the cases of sudden closures relate to travel agents dealing primarily with travel out of Singapore, which typically do not involve the hiring of local tourist guides.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In terms of impact to employees, voluntary closures are typically planned for, and travel agents usually make plans to account for their employees' welfare.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Desmond Choo suggested ring-fencing a percentage of net worth capital required for the travel agent licence, for the purpose of paying workers when travel agents close.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The minimum paid-up capital requirement was introduced with the intention of ensuring that travel agents have a certain level of financial resources before they are granted licences.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The intention was not to dictate how these funds should be used, but rather to seek broad assurance that the travel agent is unlikely to default on its obligations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In the event of sudden closures, STB works with the appropriate Government agencies to lessen the impact on employees.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Employees may also reach out to these agencies for assistance and STB can facilitate link-ups where possible.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I agree with Mr Ang Hin Kee on the importance of ensuring responsible behaviour by travel agents.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Most of our travel agents act responsibly and fulfil their obligations to customers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Our proposed amendments are a further effort to improve transparency and help consumers make more informed purchasing decisions.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: A case in point is the power that STB will have to require travel agents facing suspension or revocation to disclose this fact to their customers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: STB may also choose to publish information relating to such suspensions or revocations on their website.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To Mr Desmond Choo's query on whether there is a list of errant travel agents, consumers can access STB's TRUST platform to check the status of the travel agent they are transacting with, including whether the travel agent has had its licence suspended or revoked.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Desmond Choo has suggested to include a list of travel agents with chequered customer service records.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: To clarify, the policy intent of the travel agent legislation is to take action against errant travel agents, rather than to police all service-related issues.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: That said, the Travel Agents Regulation does address more egregious service issues, such as the need to inform customers of any material changes to tours once a contract has been formed.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Ang Hin Kee asked if STB can set up a conciliation service to resolve disputes between travel agents and consumers or tourist guides.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For disputes between travel agents and consumers, there already exists a regulation prohibiting travel agents from wilfully refusing or neglecting to resolve such disputes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: There are also other avenues and bodies for dispute resolution between such parties.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: As for disputes between travel agents and tourist guides, STB has worked with NTUC to review the feasibility of setting up a mediation centre or conciliation service to manage such disputes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, there are only a handful of such disputes brought to STB's attention each year and they are typically resolved without the need for further mediation.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: STB is monitoring this closely and will continue discussions with NTUC and other relevant agencies.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: At the same time, we are already exploring ways to have clearer contractual terms between travel agents and tourist guides, which may help reduce the occurrences of such disputes.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: While we have made a number of amendments to improve consumer protection, we also need to ensure that our travel agents are not subjected to excessive regulatory burden.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan has asked if the Government would consider requiring travel agents to provide a performance bond, so that consumers can have confidence that the travel agent will fulfil its obligations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked if MTI or STB will consider establishing a Travel Industry Compensation Fund, which can provide reimbursement to travellers in specific situations, such as travel agent insolvency.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Travel agents are also likely to pass on such increased business costs to consumers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In addition, such measures may duplicate the coverage provided by travel insurance, which a majority of consumers are already purchasing.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: STB will also continue to work closely with industry stakeholders to encourage the uptake of travel insurance via consumer education efforts.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We hope that these measures will help to enhance consumer protection, without increasing business costs significantly for travel agents.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Whether consumers can terminate their contracts with a travel agent will depend on the cancellation terms and conditions of each contract, which will apply even when the travel agent is facing suspension or revocation.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Via the Travel Agents Regulations, we intend to require travel agents to make clear the cancellation terms and conditions before entering into a contract with consumers.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Consumers will, thus, be fully aware of their rights under the contract before they sign it.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I agree with Mr Desmond Choo that it is important for the public and industry players to know which types of travel entities will now be exempted.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: STB will be raising awareness among the travel industry and the general public on this matter.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked if we could make it compulsory for exempted entities to register themselves with STB, so that we retain some degree of oversight over their activities.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We wanted to allow more room for "off-the-beaten-track" tours to grow and bring vibrancy to our tourism landscape, as Mr Desmond Choo highlighted.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: This is why we have exempted walking tours or cycling tours from needing a travel agent licence, as these tours typically do not collect significant prepayments from customers and, in some cases, none at all.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: However, I should also point out that if these tours are targeted at tourists and involve remuneration for the guiding services provided, these tours will still need to be led by licensed tourist guides.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The tourist guide licensing framework gives STB some regulatory oversight and enforcement powers against irresponsible behaviour.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Even as these entities are exempted, consumers can continue to reach out to CASE and STB if they require assistance.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Louis Ng asked if the Travel Agents Act and this Bill would include emerging models like Airbnb Experiences, Tripadvisor and Wego.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan also asked who regulates online travel entities in general, whether the Singapore Government can consider regulating them and how consumers may recover their prepayments if these online entities cease operations.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Whether an online entity falls within the jurisdiction of Singapore's legislation largely depends on whether it has physical presence in Singapore for the supply of travel products.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: For instance, if an online entity with physical presence in Singapore contracts with consumers for the supply of a travel product or sells or arranges tours in Singapore, the entity will require a travel agent licence.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: In such cases, STB has been running consumer education campaigns to increase consumer awareness of measures they can undertake to protect their interests.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will also continue to encourage consumers to purchase travel insurance to safeguard against unforeseen travel inconveniences.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Ang Hin Kee highlighted that as the travel industry transforms, we also need to ensure that our travel agents and tourist guides upskill and keep up with the times.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We have been encouraging manpower upskilling, technology adoption and greater innovation and productivity in the industry.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Employees can also tap on STB's Training Industry Professionals in Tourism fund to send their staff for further training and professional development.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked how STB is ensuring that the skills of tourist guides are tested.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The MRC keeps tourist guides abreast of new tourism industry developments, while ensuring that they continue to be equipped with appropriate guiding skills to deliver quality visitor experiences.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Our tourist guides also continue to benefit from a wide range of professional development courses.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Earlier this year, STB published a prospectus covering 64 courses by 12 training providers, with the courses touching on a wide range of topics, including storytelling skills, intercultural training, guiding skills and Singapore's art, culture, heritage and even nightlife scene.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: There is also a range of subsidies that cover up to 95% of the course fees.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: I encourage our tourist guides to utilise these resources fully.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We agree with Mr Desmond Choo that it would be useful if training can be conducted online and are exploring if this can be implemented.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: The majority of our travel agents conduct their businesses responsibly and are important players in our tourism ecosystem that connects Singapore and Singaporeans with the rest of the world.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: We will also continue with our consumer education efforts to raise awareness of the measures consumers can take to protect themselves and to communicate the intent and implications of the legislative amendments we are making now.

speaker: Ms Sim Ann
text: Lastly, the Government will continue to work with all industry stakeholders to drive capability development within the travel agent and tourist guide industries, so that employers, workers and freelancers can all keep up with a rapidly changing tourism industry and reap benefits, as Mr Desmond Choo has also mentioned.
